_meta.indication: XADAGO is a monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B) inhibitor indicated as adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing "off" episodes
_meta.receipt_date: December 29, 2015 (original NDA); resubmission (complete response amendment) dated September 21, 2016

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 016 (also referred to as Study 16 / Study 1)
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-national, 24-week study; patients randomized to XADAGO 50 mg/day, 100 mg/day, or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: PD patients experiencing "OFF" Time during treatment with carbidopa/levodopa and other PD medications (advanced/late-stage PD)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in total daily "ON" Time (without troublesome dyskinesia)
pivotal_trials.n: n=645 randomized (50 mg n=217; 100 mg n=216; placebo n=212)
pivotal_trials.result: Increase in "ON" Time vs placebo: 50 mg LS difference 0.50 hours (95% CI 0.03, 0.96; p=0.0356); 100 mg LS difference 0.53 hours (95% CI 0.07, 1.00; p=0.0238)

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-national, 24-week study; patients randomized to XADAGO 100 mg daily or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Advanced/late-stage PD patients experiencing "OFF" Time on stable carbidopa/levodopa with or without other PD medications
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in total daily "ON" Time (without troublesome dyskinesia)
pivotal_trials.n: n=549 randomized (100 mg n=274; placebo n=275)
pivotal_trials.result: Increase in "ON" Time vs placebo (efficacy analysis N=270): LS difference 0.99 hours (95% CI 0.58, 1.39; p<0.001); reduction in "OFF" time LS difference -1.06 hours (95% CI -1.43, -0.69; p<0.001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence on XADAGO 100 mg/day at least 2% greater than placebo) were dyskinesia, fall, nausea, and insomnia. Dyskinesia incidence was 21% (50 mg/day), 17% (100 mg/day) vs 9% (placebo).
target_moa: XADAGO is an inhibitor of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B); inhibition of MAO-B blocks catabolism of dopamine, thought to increase dopamine levels and dopaminergic activity in the brain. It has more than 1000-fold selectivity over MAO-A.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; safinamide is the third selective MAO-B inhibitor approved in the US (after rasagiline and selegiline) for an identical population, and no safety or effectiveness concerns needed advisory committee input.

summary.text: XADAGO was approved as a resubmission responding to a March 28, 2016 Complete Response letter (issued over deficiencies in the abuse-potential assessment); those deficiencies were addressed and the drug was recommended for approval as adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's disease patients experiencing "off" episodes, with no advisory committee meeting held and a single BCRP drug-interaction postmarketing requirement.

Therefore, I recommend approval of safinamide as adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing "off" episodes.
The sponsor should be required to conduct a clinical pharmacology study to evaluate the possibility of a drug-drug interaction between safinamide and BCRP substrates, as a Postmarketing Requirement.
